QuestionStmt.S: If $\vec{F} = (5\hat{i} - 10\hat{j})$ and $\vec{r} = (4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j})$, then the torque acting on the object will be

Solution.S:
Given:

$\vec{F} = 5\hat{i} - 10\hat{j}$

$\vec{r} = 4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j}$

Step 1:
Torque ($\vec{\tau}$) is given by the cross product:

$\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F}$

Step 2:
Write vectors in component form:

$\vec{r} = 4\hat{i} + (-3)\hat{j} + 0\hat{k}$

$\vec{F} = 5\hat{i} + (-10)\hat{j} + 0\hat{k}$

Step 3:
Use the determinant method for cross product:

$\vec{\tau} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 4 & -3 & 0 \\ 5 & -10 & 0 \end{vmatrix}$

Step 4:
Expand the determinant:

$\vec{\tau} = \hat{i}((-3)(0) - (0)(-10)) - \hat{j}((4)(0) - (0)(5)) + \hat{k}((4)(-10) - (-3)(5))$

$\vec{\tau} = \hat{i}(0 - 0) - \hat{j}(0 - 0) + \hat{k}(-40 + 15)$

$\vec{\tau} = 0\hat{i} - 0\hat{j} - 25\hat{k}$

$\vec{\tau} = -25\hat{k}$

Final answer:

The torque acting on the object is $-25\hat{k}$

Therefore, the correct option is D.
